rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: status with an expired trusted CA (errors []) expected:<502> but was:<200>
rows.note: trustCertificates(expiredCaPem) where the given certificate is an expired self-signed private CA (keytool -startdate 2000/01/01 -validity 2, bc:c) and the backend presents only its currently valid leaf for localhost: the request reaches the backend (200). ValidityCheckingTrustManager calls checkValidity only on the presented chain, and PKIX does not check the trust anchor's validity, so an expired given anchor is never checked. Contradicts AC-3 (an expired trusted self-signed certificate gives 502), the requirement text ('certificate chain is still validated (signature and validity period)') and the guide's sentence 'An expired certificate gets 502 (CONNECT_FAILED) even when it is a given one' / '만료된 인증서는 넘긴 인증서라도 502' in docs/api/en/proxy.md and docs/api/proxy.md (FR-PROXY-022 AC-7 promise). Node's https ca (OpenSSL) rejects an expired root. Fix direction: check validity of the anchor the chain ends at (e.g. every given certificate that is the issuer of the last presented certificate, or all given certificates at the call/handshake), or narrow the docs.

rows.evidence: java.lang.AssertionError: a CERTIFICATE block whose DER is a certificate plus 6 trailing bytes was accepted
rows.note: A CERTIFICATE block whose base64 decodes to a valid certificate DER followed by 6 extra bytes (04 04 'junk') is accepted: CertificateFactory.generateCertificate reads one TLV from the stream and ignores the rest, and TrustedCertificates.fromPem does not check the stream is exhausted. AC-4 requires a block whose DER does not parse to throw IllegalArgumentException at the call. Low security impact (the trusted certificate is exactly the parsed one), but the parser is not strict. Fix direction: compare the parsed certificate's getEncoded() length with the decoded byte count, or check the ByteArrayInputStream has no bytes left.

Base64.decode rejects 'AAAA=', non-canonical 'AB=='/'AAB=', 'AA=A', 'A===', 'AAAAA', 'AA==AA==', '-', '====', 'Zg=', NBSP and NUL; round-trips random 1..199-byte inputs from the MIME encoder exactly. Unpadded input ('AAA') is accepted, which is harmless.
A not-yet-valid (startdate +10d) trusted self-signed certificate gives 502 and no request byte reaches the backend.

The wrapper rejects an unrelated chain in checkServerTrusted and checkClientTrusted (delegation exceptions propagate), accepts the given certificate, and getAcceptedIssuers returns exactly the one given certificate (no system CA fallback).

With the trustCertificates factory (non-extended X509TrustManager wrapper) and SSLParameters endpoint identification HTTPS, the JDK handshake succeeds for host localhost and fails for wrong.example.invalid: the JDK's AbstractTrustManagerWrapper second layer still runs.
